isA.description: its class is the type, extends it or honours it, as PHP's `instanceof` reads it; a glob matches any of them

lines.description: it spans that many lines, its first and last among them

nameMatches.description: its name matches the regular expression

next.description: the sibling right after it passes the step

not.description: it does NOT pass the step, so a `where` can hold what only a `reject` could say

php.description: PHP's own check of the name holds — one of the checks listed below

position.description: it is the `first`, `last` or `only` one of its siblings (an only one is also first and last)

previous.description: the sibling right before it passes the step

python.description: Python's own check of the name holds

text.description: a literal's text is exactly it

textLike.description: a literal's text matches the glob

textMatches.description: a literal's text matches the regular expression

topLevel.description: it sits outside every function, closures too, and every type — code that runs when its file loads

position.description: it is the `first`, `last` or `only` one of its siblings (an only one is also first and last)

previous.description: the sibling right before it passes the step

declaredBy.description: the member it reads is declared by a class the glob names: the class its receiver holds, followed up its own parents until one declares that member. It is whose field this is, which no name can say, and it is empty — so the step keeps nothing — where the receiver has no type in the scan or no declaration of it declares the member

declaredElsewhere.description: what it names is declared in another FILE than the one it sits in, or is not with `false`. A field set from outside the file that declares it has gone around the methods its class wrote for changing itself, which is the question a rule about a type's own business asks; it holds nothing where no declaration in the scan declares what it names, so a rule says the owner too

descendant.description: some node inside it passes the step; with `"within": "ownBody"` only the nodes it holds ITSELF are stepped onto, stopping at a function nested in it, which is the difference between a method that saves and one that hands a closure holding the save to a queue

docReference.description: a doc comment names code that is GONE: a reference it makes (`<see cref>`, `{@see}`, `@see`, Sphinx `:class:`) resolves to nothing, and the project would have had to own it. Two references are left alone, which is the whole difference between this and a broken-link scanner: one the compiler could never have resolved anyway, and one whose owner is declared outside the scan, since nothing here can say whether that owner still has the member. The resolving is the bridge's own

docTag.description: its documentation carries the tag: `@tag` in PHPDoc and JSDoc, an XML element in C#, a Sphinx field or directive or a Google/NumPy section in a Python docstring

documented.description: it carries a doc comment, or not with `false`

documents.description: asked of a comment (`"select": "comment"`), the declaration the comment is written for passes the step: the node it sits above, or the node whose line it ends. A comment that documents nothing passes no step, so a rule can find the comments that are written about something and the ones that are written about nothing

duplicated.description: that many functions of the codebase, it among them, have its body, read from the tree, blind to spacing and comments

elementType.description: its type is a collection OF that type, read from a generic argument, a docblock `list<X>`, or an attribute such as `#[DataCollectionOf(X::class)]`. A collection whose element nothing says keeps nothing, since a bag of unknowns is not a bag of the type asked about

extends.description: its class extends the type directly. Its class is the one a type declaration declares, else the one the node names (`X`, `X::class`), constructs (`new X`) or holds a value of (`$this->service`, a typed parameter)

extendsAny.description: the type is anywhere in its class's chain of parents, followed through the scan and the declarations outside it the language knows; a glob (`*Service`, `[A-Z]*Repository`) matches a parent's whole name or its last part

field.description: it fills that slot of its parent in the tree — the language's own name for the slot, such as `cond`, `body`, `else`, `args` — which is the one axis of place the other checks never ask: a call standing AS a condition rather than one handed as an argument. The names are its language's, so a rule written with one judges that language

file.description: its path from the project (the repository it lies in, else the folder judged), or any tail of it, matches the glob: `*` stays within a folder and `**` crosses them, as in .gitignore

fileMatches.description: its path from the project (the repository it lies in, else the folder judged) matches the regular expression, for paths a glob cannot say, such as alternatives

hasAnnotation.description: a declaration carries the attribute or decorator

hasAttribute.description: a template element writes the attribute, plain or bound: `data-dusk` or `:data-dusk`

hasFlag.description: it carries the flag its language's tree sets

implements.description: its class honours the contract: its own, its parents', and the contracts those extend

implicit.description: the language itself calls the declaration or binds the parameter: a constructor, a magic or dunder method, Python's `self` and `cls`. Nothing the project writes calls it by that name, so a rule about how a thing is called, named or reached has nothing to say about it

inside.description: some node above it, up to the file's root, passes the step

isA.description: its class is the type, extends it or honours it, as PHP's `instanceof` reads it; a glob matches any of them

kind.description: it is the language's own kind, written as the language writes it or as the vocabulary spells it: `Expr_StaticCall` and `static-call` are one construct. The spellings are derived from the kinds, so the editor's own completion lists what a language really emits, and a spelling two kinds share is the spelling of neither

ladderRungs.description: its ladder has that many rungs AND every one compares the same subject with a constant, which is the shape whose answer is a dispatch on that subject or a lookup keyed by it. Nothing for a ladder of unrelated tests, and nothing for a branch that is itself a rung, so one ladder is counted once

layer.description: it sits in that layer of the stack the project declares (backend, Python, C#)

lines.description: it spans that many lines, its first and last among them

members.description: a type declares that many members directly that pass the step (every member, with no check); with `"inherited": true`, the members its parents and traits declare in the scan count too

name.description: its name — a call's or an access's is its name child's — is it

nameCase.description: its name, less a leading `$` or `_`, is written `camel`, `pascal`, `snake`, `upper` or `kebab` case

nameIn.description: its name is one of them

nameLike.description: its name matches the glob, `*` any run of characters and `?` one

nameMatches.description: its name matches the regular expression

nameMood.description: its name is in that linguistic mood: `bare-verb` is the verb and nothing else (`holds`, `ships`), `third-person` narrates a verb (`entersTestMode`), and `question` opens with a question word (`is`, `has`, `can`, `should`). It reads the mood, never a list of words a rule writes. It is the one check here that judges a NAME, and it answers only whether the name READS a certain way: what makes that a sin is the mood against what the thing DOES, so pair it with what the member answers or whether it changes anything, as the shipped rules do

namespaceLike.description: the namespace, package or module it is declared in matches the glob

nestedAtLeast.description: it and the nodes above it that pass the step number at least `count`

next.description: the sibling right after it passes the step

not.description: it does NOT pass the step, so a `where` can hold what only a `reject` could say

nullable.description: its type admits absence, however its language spells it: `?Money`, `Money|null`, `str | None`, `string?`, `number | undefined`. It reads the TYPE, so a union of two real types is not it and neither is a type merely named like one (`Maybe<T>`), which a glob over the text cannot tell apart. Asked of an expression it is the type the value holds, of a declaration the type it writes, and of a type node the type of the declaration it is written on; a node whose type the engine cannot read keeps nothing either way, since nothing known about a type says nothing about absence

of.description: The node the step judges in place of the one it is on: parent, enclosingFunction, enclosingType, root, closest:<kind> or child:<field>.

operator.description: its operator is exactly it: `*` and `??` tell two binary expressions apart, `+=` an assignment, `!` a unary one, `extends` a heritage clause

operatorIn.description: its operator is one of them

overrides.description: a function is a member its type owes a supertype: its language's compiler says so, or one of the same name is declared by a type it extends or a contract it honours, in the scan or outside it. It is the exemption every rule about a signature needs, since the signature is not the overriding method's to change — and it is what a name check gets wrong, where a method merely SHARING a name with another class's is nobody's to answer for

parameterType.description: a parameter's written type matches the pattern, read as returnType reads one

parameters.description: a function declares that many parameters — a variadic, a defaulted one and Python's `self` count once each

passesItsElementOn.description: a loop hands its item on to something else, every use of it; a loop whose item reaches nothing, and one that only hands the item to the method it stands in, answer no. It is the pardon the walk-the-collection rules share

php.description: PHP's own check of the name holds — one of the checks listed below

position.description: it is the `first`, `last` or `only` one of its siblings (an only one is also first and last)

previous.description: the sibling right before it passes the step

python.description: Python's own check of the name holds

redundantElse.description: its `else` stands though the taken path already left, so the else's statements can sit after it at the enclosing level; a branch whose else is the next rung of a ladder is not this. Every language answers it, from the neutral kinds and its own grammar

referredFrom.description: something referring to it — a call, a name, a written type — passes the step. It is `calledFrom` asking about the REFERENCE rather than the file it sits in, which is what tells one side of a thing from another: an event class named by a dispatch and by no listener's parameter is heard by nobody, and `{"not": {"referredFrom": …}}` says exactly that

repeated.description: that many PLACES of the codebase hold a node reading as this one does, spread over at least `files` of them (one when it says none). A place is the function the node sits in, or, where no function does, the type declaration it sits in, so a value a class declares about itself - the event a listener says it hears - is a place and two classes declaring one event are two, read from the tree as `duplicated` reads a body: blind to what a local is called and which datum a literal holds. `"exact": true` keeps both, which a repeated string literal needs; `"eitherWay": true` reads a question and its negation as one (`==` with `!=`, `is` with `is not`, `in` with `not in`); `"by": "owner"` groups by the type that declares what the left side reads, so one question about the fields of two classes that share a name is two. Anything is counted, not only a comparison: a member access of a chain counts the reach `event.data.part(X).tasks` written again and again

resolves.description: what its name refers to, resolved, is that — or, for a value that names nothing (a variable, a property), the class it holds: that exact class, not one extending it

resolvesLike.description: what its name refers to, resolved, matches the glob, or the class a value holds does: `{"resolvesLike": "*Service", "of": "child:var"}` is a receiver of any *Service

returnType.description: a function's written return type matches the pattern, spaces dropped, or the type it names resolves to; it reads the text, so `*|null` finds `int|null` — for absence itself ask `nullable` of the type, which every language answers the same way

role.description: it is that kind of thing, in the words every bridge writes: `statement`, `expression`, `member` (any declaration of a type, a function, a property or an enum case), `type` (a type as written), `pattern`, `markup` or `other`. It is how a rule says `a declaration` without naming a kind per language, which is what a rule about the order or the company of members needs

rule.description: the rule of that name finds it too, so one rule is built from another instead of repeating its checks

sameAs.description: it names the same thing as another node of the same file, reached by following `of` from it and then `target` from there — the one question a rule could not ask: a `remove` on the very collection its loop walks, an argument that is the field it was just read from. The two must be written the same, else read as the same tree; no node at the end of the path is no pass

sibling.description: a file the scan read matches the pattern, read from its file's folder: `{folder}.php` beside it, `../{folder}.php` one folder up, `{folder}` standing for the name of that folder

soleLoopBodyGuard.description: it is the WHOLE body of a loop, burying two statements or more behind its condition where a `continue` past what does not apply would keep them flat. A body that ends by leaving the loop is picking an item, and a branch that binds a name for its own body is pardoned, since inverting it would widen that name

testCode.description: it is test code, as its bridge marks it or its language names test files

text.description: a literal's text is exactly it

textLike.description: a literal's text matches the glob

textMatches.description: a literal's text matches the regular expression

topLevel.description: it sits outside every function, closures too, and every type — code that runs when its file loads

type.description: the type the expression has, as its language reads it: what a checker gave it, what its shape says, or the type its declaration writes — a primitive among them, where `resolves` answers a class alone

typeKind.description: a type declaration declares a `class`, `interface`, `enum`, `trait`, `record`, `struct` or `protocol`

typeLike.description: the type the expression has matches the glob

typeOrigin.description: its type came from there: `written` (the source's own annotation), `docblock`, `attribute`, `inferred` (the engine's own sound inference) or `compiler` (Roslyn, mypy, tsc). It is two rules nothing else can say: a type a docblock carries where the signature carries none, and the exemption `do not judge a type nobody wrote` — a reject on `inferred` leaves the engine's own reading alone

typeShape.description: its type has that shape, read from the type itself: `named`, `keyword`, `parameter`, `union`, `intersection`, `array`, `tuple`, `object`, `function`, `literal`, `pointer`, `map` or `opaque`. It is how a rule says `this answers a positional tuple` or `this hands back a bare array` without reading a type's text, and `opaque` is the honest answer for a type its bridge does not model

typescript.description: TypeScript's own check of the name holds

unnamedCondition.description: it is a logical chain standing for a concept nobody named: three parts or more asking something of two or more different OBJECTS, where a branch or a loop decides by it. It counts the objects and never the parts, since three tests of one subject are a range check; a chain a function returns is already the name that was asked for, and a guard that leaves the body says what it means by leaving

unused.description: nothing refers to it: a function or type from outside itself, through the names and calls the scan resolves and its language's call graph; a parameter, by its name read in its function; a field or property, by what reaches its declaration through the type its receiver holds, since a field refers to no symbol in most languages. A member the language itself reaches by name, and one that overrides, are not this: nothing the project writes has to name them

uses.description: its class uses the trait: itself, through a parent, or through a trait it uses

value.description: it is a literal of that very value, kind and all: the decoded value its language folded, read as the rule wrote it. `{"value": true}` is a bare `true` and NOT the string "true" nor the number 1, `{"value": 0}` is the number zero read as a number, so `0` and `0.0` are one value, and `{"value": null}` is the literal null. It is what a rule about a flag handed to a call needs, where `{"is": "literal"}` cannot tell a boolean from a label and `{"text": "true"}` matches a string that merely says so

vue.description: a Vue component's own check of the name holds — its template's, and its script's TypeScript ones

withinLoop.description: it sits inside a loop, or not with `false`

description: A commandment of the project's own: the engine it judges, the sin it names and the query that finds it.

engine.description: The engine the rule judges, or the engines: one name, or a list of them for a rule the neutral kinds let judge several.

from.description: The rule whose findings this one narrows, in place of select: an inner detector.

reject.description: Any step passing drops the node.

select.description: A neutral kind, "comment" to report on comments rather than code, or kind:<Kind> for a language's own.

fix.description: The rewrite `repent` applies to each node the rule finds; leave it out and the sin is fixed by hand.

replace.description: The text written in place of the found node; each {target} stands for the source of the node an "of" target names, hops joined by /, such as {child:left} or {child:arguments/child:body}.

substitute.description: Regular-expression substitutions applied in order to the found node's source.

with.description: What each match becomes; ${1} stands for a group.

judges.description: Folders this rule judges although the project leaves them out of "paths" or names them under "exclude", relative to the project, such as ["tests"]. They stay out of reach of every other rule. Writing it here rather than in the config keeps it with the rule, so it is not lost when the config is written again.

name.description: The sin's id, as a finding names it.

rule.description: The positive directive the fix follows.

skill.description: The slug of the skill that teaches the fix, shipped or the project's own.

suggestion.description: What to do instead, in one line.
